why: One list of asks for the two doors that decide whether 'a model from SQL' is the Model Spec: the engine's AskRoutePoint.MatchWords (run by Semanticus.Tests SqlDraftBuildTests) and the ask bar's isPlaceAsk (run by test/sql-start.test.mjs). place true means the Model Spec is the right place for the ask; false means it is about a model that already exists or is about something else. Round 6: the Model Spec route needs a REQUEST TO MAKE A MODEL: a making verb (build, create, make, start, draft, generate, set up) whose object is the model, then the source (from, out of or using ... sql), with no other change asked of that model. The verifier's round 5 asks (about a model that exists) and the plain asks it wanted are in this list, and so are the builder's own. Round 7 (verifier round 6, held-out FAIL): the rule is now the ask's INTENT (AskMakeIntent in the engine, classifyMakeIntent in the bar): a making verb, a request word, 'turn ... into a new model', the verb 'model' on a source or a bare 'new model', whose object is a model or dataset, with a source named and nothing else asked of the model. Every ask has an `intent` (what the rule says: yes, no or unsure); place is true for yes and for the one older phrase that names the wizard with no source, 'a model from scratch'. Unsure asks are the ones the words cannot settle (a model, a source and something that sounds like making one, but no main verb the rules know): the engine asks the decision service once and, with none, routes them as any other ask. The five rows that round 6 listed as not a new model and that now are (new model from my sql database, i want a new model from my sql warehouse, import my sql database as a new model, turn my sql database into a model, new model from a SQL source) are new models under the widened rule: Sol's held-out asks with the same shape (a bare new model, a request word, turn into, import as) are labelled make.
